f2.quote: Fits excluded measurements below the alloy-specific critical temperature for inertial dulling and above 873 K where the PL effect contributes.

f3.quote: Compression was conducted from 9 to 1373 K at an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10^-4 s^-1.

f4.quote: Composition-dependent local lattice distortion/MSAD and the resulting dislocation glide-resistance landscape mediate solid-solution strength; Cr-containing alloys have larger MSAD and generally stronger glide resistance.

f5.quote: At cryogenic temperatures, a reduced phonon drag coefficient permits dislocation inertial motion.

f6.quote: The PL behavior is most consistent with Cottrell-type elastic solute–dislocation attraction, particularly involving Mn and Fe; a Suzuki-segregation mechanism was not supported by the CrFeNi dissociation-width measurements but could not be definitively excluded.

f7.quote: No measurable widening of dissociated partials or reduction of stacking-fault energy was observed after high-temperature deformation of CrFeNi.

f8.quote: Relative to room-temperature deformation, cooling was expected to substantially raise CRSS

f10.quote: with the increase becoming less steep below about 77 K because of dislocation inertia.

f11.quote: Heating into the diffusion-active regime was expected to cause a small CRSS increase and serrated flow through the PL effect.
